bpe.What is byte-pair encoding, and why subw: Start from characters or bytes and repeatedly merge the most frequent pair. Subwords balance vocabulary size against sequence length and handle unseen words.
bpe.Why do modern LLMs use byte-level BPE?: Any text can be encoded with no unknown tokens: every byte has a base token.
bpe.Walk through training: counting pairs, m: Count adjacent pairs, merge the most frequent one everywhere into a new token, and repeat until the vocabulary is the target size.
bpe.How is encoding a new string done with t: Apply the learned merges in the order they were learned. A different order gives a different tokenization.
bpe.How do you break ties between equally fr: Pick the lexicographically smallest pair, or the first seen. Any deterministic rule works if it is documented.
bpe.How does vocabulary size trade sequence: A bigger vocabulary gives shorter sequences but a larger embedding table and softmax, and rarer tokens.
bpe.What problems do tokenizers cause for ar: Numbers split inconsistently, whitespace and indentation in code, and non-English text using many more tokens.

contrastive_loss.What is InfoNCE, and how does it relate: Pull matched pairs together and push others apart with a softmax over similarities. CLIP pairs images with text; SimCLR pairs augmented views.
contrastive_loss.Why do in-batch negatives work?: The other items in the batch are cheap, mostly unrelated examples, so they serve as negatives.
contrastive_loss.How do you build the similarity matrix a: Normalize the embeddings, compute sim = a @ b.T / temperature. The targets are arange(B) (the diagonal).
contrastive_loss.Why normalize embeddings, and what does: Normalizing gives cosine similarity. Temperature scales the logits: lower is sharper, focusing on hard negatives.
contrastive_loss.What makes the CLIP loss symmetric?: Average the image-to-text and text-to-image cross-entropies.
contrastive_loss.How does batch size affect contrastive l: Larger batches give more negatives and better representations. Across GPUs, all-gather the embeddings.
contrastive_loss.What goes wrong with false negatives in: Semantically matching items get pushed apart as negatives. Mention soft targets or deduplication.

mamba_ssm.What is a state space model, and what do: A linear recurrence over a hidden state. Mamba makes the parameters (delta, B, C) depend on the input.
mamba_ssm.Why does selectivity matter compared wit: Fixed SSMs process every token the same way. Selectivity lets the model choose what to remember or ignore.
A_bar = exp(delta * A); B_bar is approximately delta * B. delta controls how much each step moves the state.
mamba_ssm.What are the shapes of the hidden state: The state is (batch, d_inner, d_state). Each step updates it with A_bar * h + B_bar * x.
mamba_ssm.How does training use a parallel scan in: The recurrence is associative, so a parallel prefix scan computes all steps in O(log T) depth.
mamba_ssm.Mamba versus attention: long-context eff: Mamba is linear-time with a constant-size state. Attention recalls exact tokens but costs quadratic time.
mamba_ssm.Why are hybrid SSM and attention models: They combine cheap long context from SSM layers with the exact recall of a few attention layers.
